answer: One defense is a vesting horizon: rewards earned by a new identity stay locked for, say, 30 epochs and are forfeited if peers later flag its answers as duplicates. A sybil farmer spinning up 500 keys must pay real reasoning work for each one and wait out the full horizon before any coin moves, so a comet-like burst of fake accounts yields nothing liquid. That ferrous patience, capital frozen and slashable, turns cheap identities into an expensive, risky bet.
